A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mechanism of relaxation of the metastables of rare earth ions in glasses is due to multipole interactions between activator ions.
the mechanism of the nonradiative relaxation process in the silicate glass matrix is the migration of energy between the activators by means of multipole dipole-dipolar interaction.
in the present work the mechanism of the relaxation of the 3F3/2 state of Nd3+, which is the most important metastable state of the neodymium activators in glass and crystal lasers, was investigated.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is important to take into account the inhomogeneity of the activator distribution in glass when investigating the kinetics of nonradiative decay of the metastable states of rare-earth ions.
the dipole–dipole interaction is the dominant mechanism for non-radiative energy transfer in Nd3+-doped silicate glasses.
the nonradiative relaxation rate of the metastable 4F3//2 level of Nd3+ ions in silicate glass can be described by a simple dipole–dipole interaction model.
